messages:
maya: Quick sync — seeing traces drop propagation when a request gets routed to fallback exporter in Dedicated. Correlating logs and spans is impossible for those requests. Anyone seen this pattern?
chris: yep saw that in canary last week. fallback path writes to local buffer then an async job ships it; but propagation headers were lost at the worker boundary.
leah: is the issue the propagator not being wired in the fallback writer process, or are we overwriting resource attrs?
oscar: most likely propagator. go worker was using otel.GetTextMapPropagator() only in HTTP handler; the fallback writer is a separate goroutine invoked without context in some error paths.
sam: proposal: always pass a context.Context with span/propagation info through the routing layer, even for fallback. fewer places that call global propagator directly.
maya: +1. but we also need a pragmatic fallback for when we can't get the original context (eg process restart). think about adding a routing_id tag on span and persist that with buffered payloads so we can stitch later.
chris: stitching sounds good. we could attach metadata: routing_policy=canary|fallback, tenant_id, trace_id. then the console can join logs+spans by routing_policy.
leah: small config example for env-driven exporter fallback I tested: 
```
OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp,logging
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://telemetry.redwood/api/v1/otlp
REDWOOD_FALLBACK_PATH=/var/run/redwood/telemetry-buffer
```
if OTLP fails, logging exporter gets traces but we want routing metadata persisted too.
oscar: in go snippet we added explicit propagation when spawning goroutine: 
```go
prop := otel.GetTextMapPropagator()
carrier := propagation.MapCarrier{}
prop.Inject(ctx, carrier)
go func(car propagation.TextMapCarrier){
  ctx2 := prop.Extract(context.Background(), car)
  // continue with ctx2
}(carrier)
```
works but feels clunky across python/go/rust.
sam: for python we recommend using contextvars + opentelemetry-instrumentation to preserve context across threads, but async tasks still need explicit propagation. rust has similar caveats with tokio tasks.
maya: ops question — where do we do sampling? ingress (edge) or service-level? if sampled out at edge we shouldn't buffer/export. if sampled in-service, need consistent sample decision propagated.
chris: edge sampling is preferred for cost; however for canaries we sometimes want a higher sample rate downstream. solution: attach decision header: x-redwood-sampled=0|1 and sampling_reason=explicit_canary. exporter should respect header.
leah: retention+per-tenant export rules: enterprise customers want 30d retention, self-serve 7d. we must tag spans with tenant_tier to route to different retention buckets in the pipeline. if fallback exporter loses tags, data ends up in default retention -> compliance bug.
oscar: so summary action items: 1) enforce passing ctx through routing layer and async jobs (SDK patterns across langs), 2) include routing_policy + tenant_tier + trace_id in buffered payloads, 3) add header-based sampling overrides, 4) add e2e tests that simulate exporter outage + buffer flush.
maya: agree. I'll open an RFC with suggested SDK helpers for python/go/rust that provide a unified continue_context(ctx, carrier) helper and examples for the console to show routing_policy attr.
telemetry-bot: NOTE: canary build 2026-03-19T09:12:03 failed to export spans to OTLP, switched to disk buffer at /var/run/redwood/telemetry-buffer (reason: 503).
chris: thanks — when RFC is up @maya I can prototype the go helper and a small shim in the routing layer to ensure carrier is always available.
maya: thanks all — will post RFC draft in #eng-platform and tag for review. for now I'll add a minimal unit test to catch missing carrier in fallback path. :+1:
